jobs.title: Environmental Planning and Permitting Lead
jobs.description:
Build your team in Tennessee for HMB! We are looking for an Environmental Planning and Permitting
Division Lead
in Tennessee to join our team.

At the core of our vision is a commitment to being market leaders with engaged professionals that have the initiative, tools and opportunities to be their best.

Key Responsibilities

Lead the business development, operations and production effort for Environmental Planning and Permitting market
Fee proposals, Scope of Work, Budgeting, Invoicing, Financial Forecasting
Aid in the development of NEPA documents and/or permit applications
Assist staff in environmental planning and permitting
Collaborate with other disciplines and clients to complete projects
Ensure projects comply with applicable local, state and federal guidelines and codes
Hire and guide junior staff by providing direction and constructive feedback to support the market
Act as point of contact for Environmental Planning & Permitting
Development of project work plan and scope of work, manage projects and client relationships
Administer quality assurance for project deliverables
Maintain effective communications with clients and project teams
Ensure staff resources are deployed in a productive and profitable manner
Conduct regular meetings to ensure project needs are balanced with staff availability

Skills, Knowledge And Expertise

BS/MS in Civil Engineering, Biology, Archaeology, Geology, Natural or Environmental Sciences or related field
10+ years of professional experience in NEPA and/or permitting
Ability to review environmental documents for technical and regulatory completeness
Demonstrated knowledge of all levels of NEPA and/or the environmental permitting process
Knowledge of environmental regulations and ability to interpret and apply them in project-specific context
Experience working with state and federal regulatory agencies
Proficiency with MS Office Suite, Adobe products and GIS
Experience in Leadership, Business Development, Client Management, Project Management and Production
Possess a proven history of meeting project deadlines and budgets
Ability to guide junior staff as well as participate in environmental planning and permitting

Benefits

Excellent compensation package
Flexible work schedule
Ability to work hybrid work schedule
Competitive holiday and paid-time-off programs
401(k) Plan and Match
Competitive health, vision and dental insurance premiums
Company-furnished life insurance
Short and Long-term Disability
Parental Leave
Variety of voluntary benefit options
Employee Assistant Program (EAP)
Flexible Spending Account
and More

Pay Transparency

The base salary range for this role is indicated in the posting. This range reflects the company’s good faith estimate of the compensation for this position at the time of posting. Final compensation will be determined based on factors such as experience, skills, qualifications, internal equity, and geographic location.

jobs.title: Environmental Control Officer (ECO) Cum ECMO
jobs.description:
Job Responsibilities

Ensure effective implementation of the Environmental Monitoring and Management Plan (EMMP) across all phases of the project.
Conduct regular site inspections to monitor compliance with environmental requirements related to air quality, water management, noise control, and waste disposal.
Identify, report, and recommend corrective actions for any non-compliance or potential environmental breaches.
Maintain accurate and up-to-date environmental documentation, including inspection records and statutory reports.
Liaise with regulatory bodies such as NEA, PUB, NParks, and others to ensure full compliance with environmental legislation and permit conditions.
Conduct site briefings and toolbox talks to promote environmental awareness among workers and subcontractors.
Review and provide input on environmental method statements, risk assessments, and pollution control measures.
Supervise the implementation and maintenance of pollution control systems (e.g., silt fences, wheel wash bays, oil interceptors).
Respond to environmental emergencies (e.g., spills or complaints) and ensure proper containment, mitigation, and reporting actions are taken.
Participate in audits and support continual improvement of environmental management practices on site.

Job Requirements

Registered Environmental Control Officer (ECO) by NEA .
Minimum 2 years of relevant working experience in construction or infrastructure projects ECO cum ECMO.
Sound knowledge of local environmental regulations, codes of practice, and EMMP requirements.
Strong communication and reporting skills, with the ability to liaise with authorities and project stakeholders.
Ability to conduct site inspections independently and resolve environmental issues proactively.
Familiarity with environmental monitoring tools and reporting systems is an advantage.

jobs.title: Senior Geospatial Backend Engineer
jobs.description:
We are looking for someone who already does production geoprocessing in Python - rasterio, geopandas, numpy - and wants the geospatial layer to be the product rather than a chore buried under someone else's roadmap.

M33 is building iris
. You can ask a spatial question in plain language - "vegetation change along this corridor over the last three years" - and iris composes a real, inspectable pipeline against satellite imagery and open vector data, which you can open, change and re-run. All orchestrated with trusted tools, with transparency and provenance about what’s happening all the way through.

We are a small but growing team. You would be joining as our second engineer, and as another geospatial specialist - so we need someone who can function as a subject-matter expert as much as a developer.

The engagement

Independent contract, not employment. Remote, anywhere you can legally invoice as a business. Up to 40 hours a week at your own schedule, with at least 8 overlapping North American hours.

US$45-55/hour
, depending on depth and location.

What you would own

Our Python processing engine - the catalog of composable geoprocessing tasks iris builds pipelines from.
Making a wrong answer hard to ship quietly. Nodata that survives masking, resampling and band maths. Reprojection that does not silently degrade. Pipelines that don’t run green if they’re returning a plausible but wrong number.
Letting someone bring their own data into a pipeline, validating it, and refusing it loudly when it cannot be trusted.
Cloud-native formats and access: COGs, STAC, GeoParquet, PostGIS, DuckDB spatial, dynamic tile serving.
New data sources and connectors - satellite collections, global vector sources, disaster-event feeds.

What we need to see

Production
experience with rasterio, geopandas and numpy. (This one is non-negotiable - substantial real work, not passing familiarity.)
A spatial problem you took end-to-end into production. Any industry: agriculture, disaster response, urban planning, logistics, environmental monitoring. What matters is that you worked through the geoprocessing and shipped something that ran.
Depth underneath those libraries - GDAL internals, coordinate systems and reprojection, raster and vector operations, STAC.
Python you would be happy for someone else to maintain, and comfort working in Docker.
The independence to set technical direction rather than wait to be told what to build.

Nice to have:
SAR or optical remote sensing, spectral indices, change detection, terrain and hydrology. Performance tuning of large raster reads. Knowing how you would prove a server does what it says it does.

How to apply

Use the link to access our (short!) application form. Tell us who you are, and one spatial problem you took into production. If you look like you might be a good fit for M33, we’ll reach out for an interview.
